Problem

sampled_prs.title: fix(core): generate file operation metric in replace tool
sampled_prs.author: SaschaHeyer
sampled_prs.body:
The replace tool (edit.ts) was not generating a gemini_cli.file.operation.count metric, leading to incomplete telemetry for file modifications. This was because it only called logFileOperation from the logging service, not recordFileOperationMetric from the metrics service.
This change aligns the replace tool's behavior with the write_file tool by adding a call to recordFileOperationMetric. This ensures that partial file edits are correctly tracked in telemetry, providing a complete picture of all file modification operations.
Fixes #7391

sampled_prs.title: feat(keypress): implement Ctrl+C exit handling with confirmation
sampled_prs.author: TreeTreeDi
sampled_prs.body:
TLDR
Implements global double Ctrl+C exit behavior in KeypressContext to fix Issue #8648. Now pressing Ctrl+C once shows "Press Ctrl+C again within 3 seconds
to exit" and pressing twice safely exits, regardless of UI state (dialogs, auth screens, etc.).
Dive Deeper

sampled_prs.author: abhipatel12
sampled_prs.body:
TLDR
Fixes #10728.
This PR modifies the fallback mechanism in WebFetchTool to respect the Content-Type HTTP header of the fetched resource. Previously, html-to-text conversion was applied unconditionally to all responses in the fallback path, which corrupted non-HTML data such as JSON APIs or raw source code files.
Now, html-to-text conversion is only applied if the Content-Type indicates HTML or is missing. For all other content types, the raw text content is returned.

Summary
This pull request introduces a new architecture for pluggable authentication providers for MCP servers. It allows users and extensions to define custom authentication logic in external modules, enabling support for a wide variety of authentication schemes beyond the CLI's built-in providers. This change is primarily motivated by the need to support Google ID Tokens for services like Cloud Run, which was not possible with the previous implementation.
Details
Key changes include:

Pluggable Auth Configuration: A new auth object can be added to an MCP server configuration in settings.json

TLDR
Fixes a crash (unhandled EPIPE error) in the CLI that occurs when a hook process exits before the CLI finishes writing input to its stdin. This race condition was causing flaky failures in nightly releases on slower runners.

When HookRunner spawns a child process (e.g., a simple echo command as a hook), it attempts to write the tool's execution context (as a JSON string) to the child's stdin.

sampled_prs.author: yuvrajangadsingh
sampled_prs.body:
Summary
This PR fixes issues #15874 and #15873 where closing the terminal window causes orphaned Gemini CLI processes to spin at 100% CPU, making the system unresponsive.
Root Cause
When a terminal is closed, the shell sends SIGHUP to child processes. Without proper signal handling, the CLI process continues running but loses its controlling terminal, causing it to spin in a tight loop trying to read from a closed TTY.
Solution
This PR implements a two-layer defense:

Signal Handlers (setupSignalHandlers): Handles SIGHUP, SIGTERM, and SIGINT signals with graceful shutdown
TTY Check (setupTtyCh

sampled_prs.body:
Summary
The isSafeRegExp() heuristic in packages/core/src/policy/utils.ts incorrectly rejects patterns where a group with an inner quantifier is followed by ?. For example, (?:(.*?)\s+)? is flagged as unsafe even though ? (0 or 1) cannot cause exponential backtracking — only unbounded quantifiers (+, *, {n,}) can.
This makes it impossible to write practical commandRegex policies for CLI tools that need optional capture groups (e.g. blaze\s+(?:(.*?)\s+)?(build)\s+(.*)), as reported in #21415.

sampled_prs.title: fix(cli): resolve Ghostty/raw-mode False Cancellation in oauth flow
sampled_prs.author: Aarchi-07
sampled_prs.body:
Summary
The stdinHandler in oauth2.ts uses data.includes(0x03) to detect Ctrl+C during the OAuth browser flow. This checks if 0x03 (ETX) appears anywhere in an incoming stdin buffer.
When the CLI runs in raw mode (via Ink's TUI), every raw byte passes through unfiltered. Terminals like Ghostty and VS Code terminal (WSL + Companion extension) emit control/escape sequences during initialization or resize events that contain 0x03 as an embedded byte — not as an actual Ctrl+C keystroke — triggering a false-positive cancellation with the error 'cancelled by user'.
Related Issues
Fixes #24745

Clipboard image paste (Ctrl+V with an image) silently fails on WSL2 because getUserLinuxClipboardTool() checks XDG_SESSION_TYPE to pick between wl-paste (Wayland) and xclip (X11). sampled_prs.title: fix(core): strip login/interactive shell wrappers in stripShellWrapper
sampled_prs.author: ChristianTeroerde
sampled_prs.body:
stripShellWrapper only recognised a bare -c after sh/bash/zsh, so login/interactive command wrappers — bash -lc "...", bash -ic "...", bash -l -c "...", bash --login -c "..." — were returned unchanged.
The policy engine only re-checks a wrapped payload when the wrapper is stripped (stripped !== subCmd in policy/policy-engine.ts). For the login/interactive forms the wrapper wasn't stripped, so the inner command was never re-evaluated against the command allowlist: with bash on the allowlist, bash -lc "rm -rf ~" ran without confirmation while bash -c "rm -rf ~" correctly re-prompted. isDangerous

quotes.author: ChristianTeroerde
quotes.text: Thanks for the review — addressed both in 7f73fea.   Option-group suffix. Adopted -[il]*c so the -c command-string flag must be the last character in the group. One clarification for the record: I tested bash -ci "echo X" and zsh -ci "echo X", and both run the next-word command (echo X), not i — the "executes i" behaviour is specific to strict-getopt sh. Either way -ci/-cl are non-canonical (POSIX Utility Syntax Guideline 5) and shell-dependent, so not stripping them is the safe choice: they now fall through to the shell-level policy check (fail-closed) instead of being fine-grain re-checked.

Gemini CLI Lacks Authentication Capability for HTTP Transports: Based on a thorough review of the provided gemini-cli source code and documentation, there is no built-in mechanism to send a Bearer Token or any other authentication header when connecting to an MCP server via an httpUrl or url (SSE) transport.
The MCP server configuration object, defined in packages/cli/src/config/settings.ts, does not have a property to specify headers or tokens.
The client connection logic in packages/core/src/tools/mcp-client.ts only uses the URL and timeout to establish the c

quotes.author: swissspidy
quotes.text: It's possible to add custom headers according to the documentation, have you tried that? {   "mcpServers": {     "httpServerWithAuth": {       "httpUrl": "http://localhost:3000/mcp",       "headers": {         "Authorization": "Bearer your-api-token",         "X-Custom-Header": "custom-value",         "Content-Type": "application/json"       },       "timeout": 5000     }   } }

quotes.author: jackwotherspoon
quotes.text: @Jboner-Corvus I am going to close this out as like @swissspidy mentioned, you can pass headers to httpUrl (streamable-http) MCP servers. If this does not fix the issue, please re-open and we will take another look for you 😄

quotes.author: admackin
quotes.text: @jackwotherspoon this doesn't work (I just checked) for SSE-based MCP servers which require auth headers though, such as this one, so I think the original issue is valid. You can send auth headers to an httpUrl server and get a 405, or set up an SSE server and get a 401 because the url server type seems to ignore the header config. Can we please re-open the issue?

quotes.author: jackwotherspoon
quotes.text: @admackin Good call out, looks like headers were only added to httpUrl. Re-opened and updated title to properly reflect this 👍

The easiest way to do this is to add the --yolo command to gemini: echo "Run command 'make terraform-plan'" | gemini --yolo Which will enable all of our tools without confirmation in headless mode. You should be careful about doing this without also using some kind of sandbox. You can also use the coreTools setting to specify which tools you want to be able to run in non-interactive mode.

sampled_issues.title: Create version agnostic base model configs
sampled_issues.author: joshualitt
sampled_issues.body: Today, all model configs are hardcoded to particular model strings, i.e. gemini-2.5-pro. This leads to churn and complexity when things change. We should introduce bases for inheritance that are more generic, for example, gemini-pro-latest  / gemini-flash-latest, or perhaps we just dispense with the suffix entirely, and use generic gemini-pro-base / gemini-flash-base / etc. If we do this, we can trivially change the concrete models out to whatever we wish with just a single line change to settings.json.

sampled_issues.title: Allow sub-agents to specify static model configs
sampled_issues.author: joshualitt
sampled_issues.body:
The V0 for wiring does not support static model configs for sub-agents, instead all model configs for sub-agents are registered dynamically. However, it is easier to reason about, audit, and override static model configs, so where possible we should prefer them.
At the bare minimum, we should support static model configs alongside dynamic model configs. If possible though, we should keep model configs fully orthogonal to sub-agents, and instead all sub-agents would specify exactly which model config to use.

We use a temperature bump for retries, which directly modifies the config.

sampled_issues.title: Settings should use positive statements to avoid confusion
sampled_issues.author: chrstnb
sampled_issues.body:
What happened?
The current configuration in settings uses a double negation pattern (e.g., DisableYOLO Mode: false) which is highly confusing and error-prone. Setting a negatively-named feature (like "Disable") to a negative value (false) is counter-intuitive, as it effectively means the feature is enabled ("not disabled").
To fix this, settings should be renamed using positive statements (e.g., EnableYOLO Mode or UseFuzzySearch). This makes the boolean logic simple and clear: true means the feature is ON, and false means it is OFF.
b/465686382
What did you expect to happen?
Use positive state

quotes.author: afarber
quotes.text: Looking at the code, there are actually only 2 TOML loaders (not 3 as mentioned) - packages/core/src/policy/toml-loader.ts and packages/cli/src/services/FileCommandLoader.ts. sampled_issues.title: RemainingTokenCount calculation misses candidatesTokenCount
sampled_issues.author: MJ-CJM
sampled_issues.body:
What happened?
In packages/core/src/core/client.ts, the remaining context window is calculated like this:
const remainingTokenCount =
tokenLimit(modelForLimitCheck) - this.getChat().getLastPromptTokenCount();
The problem? It only subtracts promptTokenCount, but ignores candidatesTokenCount (the model's response). After each turn, the model's output becomes part of the conversation history, but it's never counted here.
Example with tokenLimit = 1,000,000:
lastPromptTokenCount = 800,000
candidatesTokenCount = 100,000 (model response)
actual used = 900,000
CLI thinks remaining = 1,000,000 - 800,0

What happened?
When setting up the development environment natively on Windows (PowerShell/CMD), running npm run preflight hard-crashes during the linting phase. The scripts/lint.js file relies on Unix-specific shell pipelines (grep, xargs, awk, sed, and single-quote groupings) that are not natively supported by Windows. This prevents Windows contributors from cleanly installing and verifying the repository without WSL.
What did you expect to happen?
The lint.js script should successfully verify linter installations and run the linting suite natively on Windows, matching the behavior of Linux

quotes.author: abdul-makama
quotes.text: I reviewed the issues flagged by the bot, and this is not a duplicate. Those older issues (#14971, #14481, #15074) were caused by lint.js throwing an Unsupported platform/architecture error before downloading the binaries. That architecture check has already been fixed in the current main branch. This new issue occurs after the binaries are successfully downloaded. It crashes during the actual execution phase because the script relies on Unix pipelines (grep, xargs, sed) and single-quote string escapes that natively fail in cmd.exe/PowerShell. I'm opening the PR with the OS-agnostic fix now!

What happened?
On Mac running iTerm, pasting large amount of content into the input box with CMD+V (not CTRL+V) triggers a series of prompt submissions. [tested with a large chunk of code content]
Ctrl+V on Mac behaves as expected showing [Pasted Text: 335 lines] within the input box, but CMD+V behaves as described above.
[screencast]
What did you expect to happen?
Would expect Ctrl+V and Cmd+V to have the same behavior

Run gemini to enter the interactive CLI, then run the /about command.
> /about

│
│ About Gemini CLI
│
│ CLI Version

quotes.author: jwhelangoog
quotes.text: This appears to primarily be an issue within iTerm2. Ghostty does not exhibit the same behavior. From the Gemini explanation below, iTerm may be getting tripped up with control chars when CMD+V is used instead of CTRL+V (Item 2):   The difference between Ctrl+V and Cmd+V in iTerm2 boils down to how the terminal handles the system clipboard versus the terminal's internal paste mechanism. When you use Ctrl+V (the standard Unix "literal paste" or "quoted insert" trigger), iTerm2 sends the escape sequences that the Gemini CLI is looking for to enter Bracketed Paste Mode. Cmd+V, by default, often b

quotes.author: scidomino
quotes.text: This one might be hard to do. Ctrl+V is handled by the terminal without our involvement. Cmd+v requires that we send a request to paste the clipboard which the terminal can choose to honor or not. Often, the default behavior is not to honor it since this could be a massive security hole allowing programs to arbitrarily read the clipboard. I will investigate to see if there is an alternative.

quotes.author: scidomino
quotes.text: Working with the @jwhelangoog we turned on keystroke logging and determined that ctrl+v is being sent as a literally (which means that the clipboard paste is probably happening through the clipboardy library). The cmd+v is being sent as just a literal unbracketed paste which means that GCLI literally can't tell that they are pasting and we think they're just typing really fast. iterm2 should support bracketed paste so the issue might be that it isn't being enabled properly. I don't see any log messages saying bracketed paste is being turned on in the startup logs.

quotes.author: scidomino
quotes.text: Can we confirm if the Terminal may enable paste bracketing setting is enabled or disabled in your iterm2? It should be enabled by default but if it's disabled that would explain what we are seeing.

quotes.author: scidomino
quotes.text: I've verified that we always send the "enable bracketed paste" sequence so it's hard to see what else it can be. I await to hear back from @jwhelangoog

quotes.author: scidomino
quotes.text: The user confirmed that the setting was disabled. I looked through the iTerm2 code and it looks like it is enabled by default so they must have gotten it disabled somehow.

quotes.author: jwhelangoog
quotes.text: Thanks @scidomino! FIX: iTerm2 Settings > Profiles > Terminal > Terminal may enable paste bracketing > ENABLE

When connecting to an OAuth-protected MCP server using httpUrl (Streamable HTTP transport), the initial POST request for initialize succeeds with the stored OAuth token, but the subsequent GET request to open the SSE notification stream (_startOrAuthSse) does not include the Authorization header. The server returns 401 Unauthorized, which tears down the entire connection.
The OAuth flow itself completes successfully — the token is stored in ~/.gemini/mcp-oauth-tokens.json and is valid. The server responds correctly to authenticated POST requests (verified independently via curl)

sampled_issues.author: CadanHu
sampled_issues.body:
Problem
When pasting a large block of text (e.g., a Python stack trace or a long log file) directly into the interactive CLI prompt, the CLI crashes with an ENAMETOOLONG error.
The root cause is that the input parser (parseAllAtCommands in packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/atCommandProcessor.ts) identifies strings starting with @ as potential file paths and passes them to resolveToRealPath (in packages/core/src/utils/paths.ts). resolveToRealPath calls fs.lstatSync on the entire string without validating its length. If the string is longer than the operating system's maximum path length (e.g., 1024 cha

quotes.author: CadanHu
quotes.text: Additional context from the user: This issue has been persistent for at least two months. It consistently triggers when pasting backend error logs into the prompt, especially after several rounds of chat have already occurred in the session. The resulting crash (full red screen/unhandled rejection) makes long-running debug sessions very fragile.

quotes.author: CadanHu

While a previous attempt was made to fix a similar issue in PR #25009 (Issue #24898), that fix was restricted to the cli package's top-level input handling. Why the previous fix (#25009) failed: The current crash bypasses the CLI-layer length check because the atCommandProcessor identifies the pasted string as a potential @path command. quotes.author: BGMLAI
quotes.text: This is a classic confused-deputy bypass: the edit tool denied an out-of-scope write, but the shell remained powerful enough to perform the same effect. Policy must be enforced on effects across all tools, not separately per tool name. The shell sandbox should deny writes outside the workspace regardless of whether they come from Node, Python, redirection, or a helper binary. A regression should attempt the same forbidden write through multiple interpreters and assert identical denial and no file change.

quotes.author: samvallad33
quotes.text: The specific failure here — the edit tool respecting the workspace boundary while the shell path happily routed around it — is the gap between per-tool permissions and per-command gating. Operator Lite for Gemini CLI is a BeforeTool hook in settings.json that classifies every shell command through a deterministic gate before execution; scripting-language one-liners that write outside the workspace are a block class, so the Node script that rewrote your Context7 extension config would have been stopped (or, in shadow mode, at least receipted with a full record) before it ran. quotes.author: Keesan12

What happened?
The lightweight CLI bootstrap in packages/cli/index.ts reads advanced.autoConfigureMemory before loading the full settings system. When GEMINI_CLI_HOME is set, that bootstrap path looks for settings.json directly under $GEMINI_CLI_HOME.
The rest of the storage/settings layer treats GEMINI_CLI_HOME as the replacement home directory and resolves the user settings file to $GEMINI_CLI_HOME/.gemini/settings.json via Storage.getGlobalSettingsPath().

People tend to trust the tool more when it tells them exactly which config it actually read.

quotes.text: Shipping the helper prebuilt is preferable, with a signature or embedded hash verified before execution. quotes.author: BGMLAI
quotes.text: The proposed mode-at-create fix is correct, and the parent directory should also be private and protected from symlink substitution. For stronger guarantees, open with exclusive creation, mode 0600, write through the descriptor, fsync if persistence matters, and atomically replace only within a 0700 user-owned directory. A regression can run with umask 000 while another process watches the directory and assert that no world-readable inode or reusable symlink target ever appears.

sampled_issues.author: WolfGreyDev
sampled_issues.body:
What happened?
During CLI startup, settings files (system, user, workspace) are parsed, immediately expanded against process.env, and validated in a single monolithic step inside the load helper. However, local .env files (which populate process.env with workspace-specific variables) are only loaded after this settings expansion and validation step has already finished.
Because of this load-order race condition, any settings mapped to environment variables defined only in .env (such as $GITHUB_MCP_PAT) remain unexpanded when setting up Model-Context Protocol (MCP) servers.

sampled_issues.title: bug: shell execution runs exit handling twice on spawn failure ('error' and 'close' both call handleExit)
sampled_issues.author: aniruddhaadak80
sampled_issues.body:
What happened?
In the shell execution pipeline, both the child 'error' and 'close' events invoke handleExit(), and handleExit has no re-entrancy guard. Per Node's documented behavior, 'close' fires after 'error' when spawning fails — so every failed spawn runs exit handling twice: onOutputEvent({ type: 'exit', ... }) fires twice, background-history finalization runs twice, and cmdCleanup?.() executes twice. If 'error' fires mid-run on a successfully spawned child (e.g., kill/IPC failure), the result settles early on partial output before 'close' arrives.

sampled_issues.title: Nested .gitignore: patterns with only a trailing slash (e.g. build/) are anchored instead of matching at any depth
sampled_issues.author: Dev-next-gen
sampled_issues.body:
What happened?
A pattern with only a trailing slash in a nested .gitignore, such as build/, only ignores the build directory sitting next to that .gitignore. Directories with the same name further down are still returned by file discovery.
With pkg/.gitignore containing build/:

pkg/build/out.js is ignored, as expected.
pkg/tools/build/out.js is not ignored, so it still shows up through glob, ls, read_many_files, ripGrep and @ completion.

It comes from GitIgnoreParser.processPatterns in packages/core/src/utils/gitIgnoreParser.ts. For a nested .gitignore, the pattern is only prefixed with **/

quotes.author: dylanyunlon
quotes.text: I traced this down to processPatterns() in gitIgnoreParser.ts — the condition at line 93 checks !p.includes("/") to decide whether to prepend **/, but a trailing slash (like in build/) counts as a slash, so the **/ prefix is skipped and the pattern gets anchored. The gitignore(5) spec is clear on this: "If there is a separator at the beginning or middle [...] the pattern is relative to the directory level of the particular .gitignore file itself" and separately, "A trailing / matches only directories." So the trailing slash is about what can match (directories only), not where it matches (anch

quotes.author: Dev-next-gen
quotes.text: I've opened #29324 with the minimal fix described above: !p.slice(0, -1).includes('/'), plus a regression test for the pkg/tools/build/out.js case. Two files, +14 −2. #29323 addresses the same root cause with a wider scope — a new ignorePatternUtils module, an isAncestorDirectoryIgnored check in FileDiscoveryService and symlink handling in getFolderStructure. Those are separate improvements on top of the one-line correctness fix, so I kept mine narrow and would rather it be reviewable on its own. Happy to close it if you prefer the broader change.
